title: Production migration — Kaboom Crew bombers use the procbomber generator + recipe pipeline (re-promote of GDP-2026-05-21-007, now MUST)
intent: Two sprints of generator work landed (S102 + S103) and the bench produces visibly-distinct, animated, IK-driven bombers. Meanwhile the production game still uses the static `player.prefab.json` + `bot.prefab.json` capsule + sphere meshes. The deferral rationale in S102 notes ('migration is the LAST step after all generator improvements stabilise') was correct — the conditions are now met. This story replaces both prefab meshes with `procedural:procbomber` (or a kaboom-namespaced clone) backed by a CharacterRecipe lookup, wires up the same URL + agent-probe surfaces from GDP-2026-05-22-001, and migrates the bench animation systems into project-local systems on the kaboom-crew side. The original GDP-2026-05-21-007 was deferred for legitimate reasons; this re-promote bumps priority to MUST because every other character-pipeline story now depends on a real production consumer.
rationale: Sources: prior proposal GDP-2026-05-21-007 (deferred S102) + S102 notes ('migration is the LAST step after all generator improvements stabilise') + S103 notes ('after this sprint the bench should be USABLE for designing actual character recipes'). All deferral conditions met. The main game has been iterating around static placeholder bombers for ~10 sprints; the user's headline goal — 'modern network game' — depends on visibly-distinct bombers, especially in multiplayer where reading other players is the primary information channel. Marked MUST because the longer this waits, the more bench-only logic accumulates that has to be ported under pressure when multiplayer lands.
acceptanceHints: Depends on GDP-2026-05-22-001 — needs the formal CharacterRecipe serializer for URL + probe surfaces.
Code MOVE (not copy) the generator from examples/procbomber-bench/src/generators/ → examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/. The bench imports from the new location after the move; nothing duplicates.

Same for the spawner (`bomber-tree-spawner.ts`), the LimbPivots component (`limb-pivots.ts`), the two-bone-IK helper (`two-bone-ik.ts`), and the recipe formaliser (recipe.ts from GDP-001 of this batch). All live under examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/.

examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts: register the procedural-mesh keys (`procbomber-head`, `procbomber-torso`, `procbomber-upper-arm`, …) with the engine procedural-mesh registry — same registry the bench uses. The kaboom-crew side uses the SAME key prefix as the bench (`procbomber-*`) so the generator code stays single-sourced.

examples/kaboom-crew/prefabs/player.prefab.json + bot.prefab.json: REMOVE the static MeshRenderer.mesh (capsule/sphere refs). Replace with an entity-spawn convention: the prefab carries Transform + GridPosition + BomberStats + GridMover + minimap-marker as today, but the visible mesh is built by the spawner AT SPAWN TIME from a CharacterRecipe. The spawner attaches the 10-mesh + 9-pivot tree under the prefab's root entity.
Recipe sources, in priority order at spawn time:
1. Per-entity recipe explicitly set via probe / network (e.g. server-handed recipe in multiplayer mode).
2. `?recipe=<base64url>` URL — applied to player.1 (debug + agent only).
3. `?botRecipe=<base64url>` URL — applied to bot.1.
4. Fallback default: player.1 = `resolveCharacterRecipe(1)` (sky family), bot.1 = `resolveCharacterRecipe(2)` (ember family). Two visibly-distinct bombers with zero setup.

Animation pipeline migration: the bench-animation-system.ts that drives idle-bob / walk-swing / limb-test / reach in the bench BECOMES a project-local Kaboom Crew system. Naming convention: split into one file per behaviour under `examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/anim/` to match the GDP-2026-05-20-009 spec. The current bench-animation-system kinds map:
- idle-bob   → idle-animation-system.ts (always runs when GridMover.velocity = 0)
- walk-swing → walk-animation-system.ts (runs when GridMover.velocity > 0; phase advances with travelled distance, NOT wall clock — see GDP-2026-05-20-009 acceptance hints)
- reach (IK) → bomb-place-animation-system.ts (triggered by PlaceBombRequest, NOT by the bench dropdown)
- limb-test  → STAYS in the bench only (debug visualisation, not a production behaviour)

Death animation: the existing kaboom slapstick-death (S100) operates on the root Transform. After migration, it STILL runs there — the limb-pivot animations layer on top of root-Transform animation, not replace it. Document composition order in a comment block at the top of bootstrap.ts.

HUD: minimap marker colour pulls from recipe.palette.head (or family primary). This is the only player-visible recipe surface in MVP — the per-bomber identity colour. Bottom-left HUD per-bomber line stays text-only.

Existing gameplay invariants: every existing kaboom-crew test passes UNCHANGED — unit tests on bomb-placement / blast / pickup / round-resolve, the bot-vs-bot integration spec, the Playwright smoke test. The mesh swap is presentation only; rules + stats + collision rules are identical.
Recording compatibility: the deterministic recording fixture (recordings/demo-30s.recording.json) gets regenerated in this PR. Gameplay events unchanged; only the visual replay looks different.

Bench retention: examples/procbomber-bench/ stays as the dev iteration sandbox. Its bootstrap imports the generator from examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/ (no copy-paste). The bench remains the place to test recipe edge cases before they hit gameplay; production is kaboom-crew.

Agent probe surface on the kaboom side (mirrors the bench probes from GDP-001): `window.__agf.kaboom.getRecipe(entityId)`, `setRecipe(entityId, recipe)`, `setRecipeFromSeed(entityId, seed)`. Lets QA pin a specific bomber appearance for screenshot regression tests.

Acceptance smoke: `npm run dev` → /?project=kaboom-crew → player.1 (sky-family bomber) + bot.1 (ember-family bomber) visible as procedural meshes with the S103 walk-swing during movement. Difficulty preset still applies. Round resolve still works. Auto-restart still works.
Acceptance debug: `?recipe=<base64url>` → player.1 renders the specified recipe; reload with same URL produces identical mesh.
Acceptance agent: `__agf.kaboom.setRecipeFromSeed('bot.1', 99)` mid-round → bot.1's visuals swap, gameplay state preserved, no crash.

Cleanup: when a bomber entity despawns (round restart, leave-world), its 10-mesh + 9-pivot child tree is fully torn down. No Three.js leaks across rounds — verify via the existing leak-hunt recipe (`docs/agent-debug-recipes.md`).

Forward-looking (NOT in scope here, just noted): in multiplayer (GDP-2026-05-20-007), the SERVER becomes the recipe authority — it hands out recipes in the joinWorld payload. Client renders what the server says. URL recipe overrides stay client-side for solo + debug only.

Out of scope (explicit): hit-recoil / spring-sway / bomb-place-arm reach in production (those are GDP-2026-05-22-004), accessories (GDP-2026-05-22-003 — bombers ship without accessories at migration time, family + proportions + walk-cycle deliver the visual identity), texturing extras (panel seams / decals / patterns — deferred until post-migration visual review).
